paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. God gave Israel a promise before they ever set foot in the land: "After you enter the land that I am giving you as a home…" (Numbers 15:2). After the heavy news of Numbers 14, He still talks about what they'll do when they get there. He is a God who keeps His word and finishes what He starts.

Then comes the part that gets me. One law for the native-born and the foreigner, and it's "a permanent statute for the generations to come" (Numbers 15:15). When someone sins unintentionally, the priest makes atonement and "he will be forgiven" (Numbers 15:28). I've set a timer and never hit start, so I know what it is to miss it without meaning to. God made a way back for that, for the whole congregation, for one person, and for the foreigner right alongside them (Numbers 15:26, 29).

But God also draws a line. The person who sins defiantly "has despised the word of the LORD and broken His commandment" (Numbers 15:31). So here's the heart of it, friend: God's word is not something to shrug at. Hold it close, bring Him your mistakes, and keep the ovens ready!
